complexity_ledger.narrative: AC-03 is the generation-time half of the epic: a descriptor is advice until it constrains the request. It ships prompts/implementation_brief.md (with templates/implementation_brief.md as the rendered shape) and prompts/aspect_decomposition.md, in the form prompts/coverage_audit.md established, plus the case-module/feature-module distinction stated once in SKILL.md under the Program Spec Rule. ZERO model delta, as the plan expected: ticket current == desired byte for byte, TLC green reproducing AC-01's figures exactly, and all three of specs/current, ticket current and ticket desired measuring 10 variables / 16 actions / 1 component / Q = 0.000. See results/model-delta.txt. THE DEMONSTRATION. Four briefs were rendered end-to-end by following the prompt, and they are kept as evidence because the interesting result is the spread, not any one of them: * OpenTicket, specs/current under a DECLARED 2-component partition (workflow | scanners) -- DEGRADED. Real constraints: writes only ticket_state/lastCommand/result, internal to workflow so it may not touch the scanner component at all, one declared effect port (spec_tree: filesystem.write **/specs/**), does not span so one commit point, and three of the variables it writes flagged as not single-writer. * AnalyzeComplexity, same descriptor, subject component named by the caller -- DEGRADED on two counts. Same partition, but the subject component owns nothing and has no internal action, so "this work belongs to scanners" restricts nothing by itself. The strongest clause in that brief is the measured SPAN: the action commits lastCommand/result in workflow and complexity_gate in scanners in one step, and the brief says the model asserts those land atomically -- honor it or report the model wrong. * OpenTicket, specs/current under the EMERGENT partition -- REFUSED, and the refusal artifact records verbatim what the vacuous brief would have said ("component C1, 10 of 10 variables, reaches nothing, zero violations"), so the failure mode is legible rather than theoretical. * CreateAccount, examples/distributed_history/.../Internal.tla, EMERGENT -- the only FULL brief, and it clears crossing_action_fraction by exactly zero. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE EPIC'S WORKING ASSUMPTIONS, both measured here. (1) AC-01's `consumable_as_architecture` is necessary but NOT sufficient for a non-vacuous brief. It is `partition_source == "declared" or decomposes`, which is right for AC-02 -- whose question is whether the project named a boundary to compare code against -- and wrong as AC-03's only gate, because it is true for ANY declared partition including a deliberately useless one. The prompt therefore layers three per-render vacuity tests on top of it: V1 (one component) refuses; V2 (the subject component owns nothing AND has no internal action) and V3 (crossing fraction > 0.5) degrade rather than refuse, because the write-set, effect-port and atomicity clauses are measured PER ACTION and survive a bad partition intact. The two DEGRADED renders above differ by exactly V2, from the same descriptor -- whether a brief constrains anything depends on which component the work lands in, not only on the partition score. (2) "Neither real model decomposes" is not what was measured. Internal.tla decomposes EMERGENTLY (2 components, Q = 0.0069, crossing fraction 0.50), and exhaustive search finds decomposing partitions of specs/current itself. See `refinement:` above and AC-03-DF-02. The refusal doctrine survives intact -- refusing to invent a cut is still right -- but the wording claims more than a greedy search establishes. A THIRD, SMALLER FINDING, filed as AC-03-DF-01 and defended against in the prompt: for a one-component partition the JSON reports ownership.single_writer_violations as null WITH a stated reason, but components[0].owns as the bare empty list []. A consumer reads that as "owns nothing" -- a plausible architectural fact -- when it means "undefined here". The text renderer says NOT MEASURABLE; the machine-readable contract that AC-02 and AC-03 actually read does not. Gate A refuses before the field can be reached, which is why the guard is a gate and not a caveat. DOCTRINE. CD-01 holds: neither prompt proposes a cut, a refactor, a target shape or a next step. Move 3's shapes are the vocabulary the measured facts are STATED in -- the brief says "these are your declared ports", not "push effects to the edges"; "the model says these commit together", not "introduce a commit point". Both are advisory and gate nothing. The Program Spec Rule is not weakened: the aspect prompt forbids a case module from declaring any state, constant or action, requires EXTENDS over INSTANCE/LOCAL, and keeps the removal test (delete every case module and the program is still fully represented) as the rule rather than a note. WHAT IS NOT SHOWN, and both prompts say so in their own validation sections: nothing here measures whether a brief changes what a coding agent produces. The prompts make the ask derivable and checkable field by field. Whether a derivable ask yields more coherent code is an empirical question this ticket did not answer and could not -- it belongs to the epic's evaluation tickets. Until then a brief is a hypothesis with good provenance, not a result.

refinement.detail: Searched and found none that this ticket may take. AC-03 has no model delta to refine, so the search ran against the standing model, and it produced a result worth recording rather than a reduction. The obvious candidate is the one AC-01 named: specs/current has ONE emergent component at Q = 0.000, because lastCommand and result are written by all 15 commands. Splitting that god-pair would cut the interaction graph. It is not available here -- it is a production refactor of the CLI, outside AC-03's conflict keys (prompts/, templates/, references/case_modules.md, SKILL.md), and Move 3 requires explicit user approval besides. While rendering the brief this ticket measured something that sharpens the question for whoever does take it. The claim "this model does not decompose" is a claim about GREEDY modularity maximization, not about the model. Exhaustive enumeration of all 115,975 set partitions of the model's 10 variables, scored with the SHIPPED modularity function and the SHIPPED three criteria, finds TWO partitions that meet all three -- the best at Q = 0.0029 with a crossing-action fraction of 0.188 -- and the shipped CLI confirms it when the partition is handed back via --components ("the partition is a cut -- every criterion above is met"). Reproduction is checked in at results/ac03_df02_exhaustive_partition_search.py and the finding is filed as AC-03-DF-02. That is NOT a refinement to apply, and this ticket deliberately does not apply it. Q = 0.003 is negligible structure, and adopting the exhaustive search would have the tool NAME a cut the project never declared -- the exact CD-01 failure the refusal doctrine exists to prevent. What it changes is the wording of a claim the epic leans on, which is why it is a deferred finding for the owner and not a change here.

summary: AC-03: the ask -- prompts/implementation_brief.md + templates/implementation_brief.md and prompts/aspect_decomposition.md. Zero TLA+ model delta (ticket current == desired, TLC green, figures identical to AC-01). Four end-to-end renders kept as evidence: two DEGRADED briefs from this repository's own model under a declared partition, one REFUSAL from the emergent one-component partition, one FULL brief from the worked example's Internal view. consumable_as_architecture is necessary but not sufficient for a non-vacuous brief; the prompt adds three per-render vacuity tests. Two deferred findings filed (AC-03-DF-01, AC-03-DF-02).

assertions: Each prompt names its inputs (which descriptor fields), its output artifact, and what the agent may NOT do.
The implementation brief is derivable from a real architecture descriptor: demonstrate it end-to-end on this repository's own model and keep the rendered brief as evidence.
Neither prompt proposes an architectural move the descriptor did not measure (CD-01).
SKILL.md states the case-module/feature-module distinction in one place and the Program Spec Rule is not weakened.

ticket.finding: The brief renders mechanically, and it renders honestly only because it is allowed to refuse. Four end-to-end renders: this repository's own model under a hand-declared 2-component partition produced a DEGRADED brief for an internal action (OpenTicket) and a DEGRADED brief for a spanning action (AnalyzeComplexity); the same model under the emergent partition produced a REFUSAL; and examples/distributed_history/.../Internal.tla produced the only FULL brief, from an EMERGENT partition that is a cut (2 components, Q = 0.0069, crossing fraction exactly 0.50). Two corrections to the epic's working assumptions fall out. (1) AC-01's `consumable_as_architecture` is necessary but NOT sufficient for a non-vacuous brief -- it is true for ANY declared partition, including one where the subject component owns nothing and has no internal action, so the prompt adds three per-render vacuity tests on top of it. (2) The claim that no real model here decomposes is a claim about greedy search, not about the models: Internal.tla decomposes emergently, and exhaustive enumeration of all 115,975 partitions of specs/current finds 2 that meet all three shipped criteria (filed as AC-03-DF-02, with a checked-in reproduction). Neither prompt proposes a move; the implementation brief states measured ownership, ports, declared effect ports and measured atomicity spans, and the aspect prompt refuses to infer aspects the model author did not name. What remains unmeasured, and is stated in both prompts: nothing here shows a brief changes what a coding agent produces.

ticket.model_delta_result: ZERO, as expected. AC-03 adds no state variable, no action, and no invariant: prompts/implementation_brief.md, prompts/aspect_decomposition.md, templates/implementation_brief.md, references/case_modules.md and SKILL.md only. `diff -r` of ticket current/ against desired/ is empty, and both still equal the project baseline (10 variables, 16 actions, 1 emergent component, Q = 0.000 for all three). TLC on ticket current is green and reproduces AC-01's post- ticket figures exactly: 32,122,220 generated / 1,292,951 distinct / depth 26 / 57s. Evidence: results/model-delta.txt, results/tlc-ticket-current.txt.
ticket.objective: The generation-time half of the epic, and the owner's stated hypothesis: incoherent code is partly a function of how the work is ASKED for. Ship two prompts in the shape prompts/coverage_audit.md already established. (1) implementation_brief.md turns an architecture descriptor into a constrained ask: this action belongs to component C, which owns variables V; it may reach D only through port P; effects live at the boundary (functional core / imperative shell); one externally visible commitment per action. The refactor target shapes in references/architecture_tractability.md, Move 3, are the vocabulary -- this ticket makes them an instruction instead of advice. (2) aspect_decomposition.md is the BDD ask from the user's perspective: enumerate the aspects of the public surface, name each one's Given, and map each to a case module and its action scope. Reconcile both with SKILL.md's Program Spec Rule so a case module is never mistaken for a feature module.
